# Philox4x32-10 constants split so every literal used by device code fits a
# signed 32-bit integer: M0 = 0xd2511f53, M1 = 0xcd9e8d57 (multiply constants),
# W0 = 0x9e3779b9, W1 = 0xbb67ae85 (per-round key increments of Random123
# philox4x32x10).
_M0L = tl.constexpr(0x1F53)
_M0H = tl.constexpr(0xD251)
_M1L = tl.constexpr(0x8D57)
_M1H = tl.constexpr(0xCD9E)


@triton.jit
def _mul_hi_lo(a, B0: tl.constexpr, B1: tl.constexpr):
    """``(a * B) >> 32`` and ``(a * B) mod 2**32`` for uint32 ``a``, constant B.

    ``B`` is split into 16-bit halves, so only 16x16 and 32x16 products are
    needed instead of a 32x32->64 multiply-high.  The low product falls out of
    the same partial products: the low half-word of ``u0`` and the high
    half-word of the true product are both ``a0*b0``'s low half, and the high
    half-word of the product is ``w1``'s low half, so an xor of ``w1 << 16``
    with ``u0`` reproduces the low 32 bits exactly.
    """
    a0 = a & 0xFFFF
    a1 = a >> 16
    u0 = a0 * B0
    t = a1 * B0 + (u0 >> 16)
    w1 = a0 * B1 + (t & 0xFFFF)
    hi = a1 * B1 + (t >> 16) + (w1 >> 16)
    # low32 = a0*b0 + (a0*b1 + a1*b0) * 2**16 (mod 2**32): its low half is
    # a0*b0's low half and its high half is (a0*b1 + a1*b0 + a0*b0>>16) mod
    # 2**16, which is exactly w1's low half.  Both halves must be placed, not
    # xored into the existing bits of u0.
    lo = (u0 & 0xFFFF) | ((w1 & 0xFFFF) << 16)
    return hi, lo


@triton.jit
def _philox4(seed, c0, c1):
    """Philox4x32-10 over per-lane counters ``(c0, c1)``.

    Same algorithm, key schedule and round count as ``tl.philox``, which is
    scalarised on this backend (measured ~0.25 us per lane).  The whole 64-bit
    seed forms the key and the whole 64-bit generator offset forms the base of
    the lane counter, so seed bits 31..63 and offset bits 32..63 change the
    stream.
    """
    k0 = seed.to(tl.uint32)
    k1 = (seed >> 32).to(tl.uint32)
    c2 = c0 * 0
    c3 = c2
    w0 = (tl.full((), 0x9E37, tl.uint32) << 16) + tl.full((), 0xB9, tl.uint32)
    w1 = (tl.full((), 0xBB67, tl.uint32) << 16) + tl.full((), 0xAE85, tl.uint32)
    for _ in tl.static_range(10):
        hi0, lo0 = _mul_hi_lo(c0, _M0L, _M0H)
        hi1, lo1 = _mul_hi_lo(c2, _M1L, _M1H)
        c0 = hi1 ^ c1 ^ k0
        c1 = lo1
        c2 = hi0 ^ c3 ^ k1
        c3 = lo0
        k0 = k0 + w0
        k1 = k1 + w1

def uniform_kernel(
    out_ptr,
    N,
    philox_seed,
    philox_offset,
    from_,
    span,
    lo,
    hi,
    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,

    # computed on the host; both are exact in OUT_DT, so these casts are too.

    philox_offset = philox_offset.to(tl.int64)

    c1 = ((philox_offset >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32)
    c0 = c0 + tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    r0, r1, r2, r3 = _philox4(philox_seed, c0, c1)
    off = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK * 4 + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    v0 = tl.minimum(tl.maximum((uint_to_uniform_float(r0) * span + from_).to(OUT_DT), lo_dt), hi_dt)
    v1 = tl.minimum(tl.maximum((uint_to_uniform_float(r1) * span + from_).to(OUT_DT), lo_dt), hi_dt)
    v2 = tl.minimum(tl.maximum((uint_to_uniform_float(r2) * span + from_).to(OUT_DT), lo_dt), hi_dt)
    v3 = tl.minimum(tl.maximum((uint_to_uniform_float(r3) * span + from_).to(OUT_DT), lo_dt), hi_dt)
    tl.store(out_ptr + off, v0, mask=off < N, eviction_policy="evict_first")
    tl.store(out_ptr + off + BLOCK, v1, mask=off + BLOCK < N, eviction_policy="evict_first")
    tl.store(out_ptr + off + BLOCK * 2, v2, mask=off + BLOCK * 2 < N, eviction_policy="evict_first")
    tl.store(out_ptr + off + BLOCK * 3, v3, mask=off + BLOCK * 3 < N, eviction_policy="evict_first")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- dtype bounds
_HALF = {torch.float16: "e"}
_WORD = {torch.float32: "f"}


def _from_bits(bits, dtype):
    if dtype is torch.bfloat16:
        return struct.unpack("f", struct.pack("I", (bits & 0xFFFF) << 16))[0]
    if dtype is torch.float16:
        return struct.unpack("e", struct.pack("H", bits & 0xFFFF))[0]
    return struct.unpack("f", struct.pack("I", bits & 0xFFFFFFFF))[0]


def _to_bits(x, dtype):
    if dtype is torch.bfloat16:
        return struct.unpack("I", struct.pack("f", x))[0] >> 16
    if dtype is torch.float16:
        return struct.unpack("H", struct.pack("e", x))[0]
    return struct.unpack("I", struct.pack("f", x))[0]


def _round_dtype(x, dtype):
    """Nearest ``dtype`` value of ``x`` (round-half-to-even), as a float."""
    if dtype is torch.bfloat16:
        bits = struct.unpack("I", struct.pack("f", x))[0]
        top = bits >> 16
        rest = bits & 0xFFFF
        if rest > 0x8000 or (rest == 0x8000 and (top & 1)):
            top += 1
        return _from_bits(top, dtype)
    if dtype is torch.float16:
        return struct.unpack("e", struct.pack("e", x))[0]
    return struct.unpack("f", struct.pack("f", x))[0]


def _neighbour(x, dtype, up):
    """Adjacent ``dtype`` value above (``up``) or below ``x``."""
    nbits = 32 if dtype is torch.float32 else 16
    sign = 1 << (nbits - 1)
    if x == 0.0:
        # +0 and -0 are different bit patterns at the ends of their blocks.
        return _from_bits(1 if up else sign | 1, dtype)
    bits = _to_bits(x, dtype)
    return _from_bits(bits + 1 if (bits & sign == 0) == up else bits - 1, dtype)


def _sample_bounds(dtype, from_, to):
    """Representable sampling interval of ``dtype`` for the half-open ``[from_, to)``.

    A float32 draw inside ``[from_, to)`` can round *out* of the interval when
    it is stored: ``from_`` may sit between two ``dtype`` values (so the
    nearest one is below it) and ``to`` may be representable or round down.
    The kernel therefore clamps to the smallest representable value >= ``from_``
    and the largest representable value < ``to``.  ``from_ == to`` is a
    degenerate request that aten::uniform answers with a constant.
    """
    if from_ == to:
        pinned = _round_dtype(from_, dtype)
        return pinned, pinned
    lo = _round_dtype(from_, dtype)
    if lo < from_:
        lo = _neighbour(lo, dtype, True)
    hi = _round_dtype(to, dtype)
    if hi >= to:
        hi = _neighbour(hi, dtype, False)
    if lo > hi:
        hi = lo
    return lo, hi


# ------------------------------------------------------------------- launching
_MAX_BLOCK = 4096
_MIN_BLOCK = 64
# Aim for at least this many programs so a large tensor spreads over the
# vector cores; four values are produced per Philox counter.
_PROGRAM_TARGET = 160
_PLAN = {}
_DRIVER = triton.runtime.driver.active


def _plan(dtype, n, from_, to):
    key = (dtype, n, from_, to)
    plan = _PLAN.get(key)
    if plan is None:
        block = min(_MAX_BLOCK, max(_MIN_BLOCK, triton.next_power_of_2(n // _PROGRAM_TARGET)))
        grid = triton.cdiv(n, block * 4)
        lo, hi = _sample_bounds(dtype, from_, to)
        # [block, grid, lo, hi, span, direct_launcher]
        plan = [block, grid, lo, hi, float(to) - float(from_), None]
        if len(_PLAN) > 512:
            _PLAN.clear()
        _PLAN[key] = plan
    return plan


def _direct(kern, block, grid, from_, span, lo, hi):
    """Re-enter the compiled kernel, skipping per-call argument binding.

    ``kernel[grid](...)`` rebuilds and re-hashes the whole bound-argument set on
    every call, which measured ~70 us of host time here -- the entire gap to
    the reference on launch-bound sizes.  The compiled object already carries
    the entry point, the packed metadata and the specialisation for this exact
    (dtype, BLOCK, grid, N, range) shape, so re-entering it with the same
    argument vector Triton's own run() builds is equivalent.  The current
    stream is still read per call, the tensor and generator state are never
    cached, and any failure falls back to the ordinary metacall.
    """
    run = kern.run
    function = kern.function
    metadata = kern.packed_metadata
    execute = run
    get_stream = _DRIVER.get_current_stream

    def launch(out, n, seed, offset, dev):
        execute(grid, 1, 1, get_stream(dev), function, metadata, None, None, None,
                out, n, seed, offset, from_, span, lo, hi, block)

    return launch


def uniform(self, from_=0.0, to=1.0, *, generator=None):
    # aten::uniform rejects an empty interval before launch; mirror that so
    # from > to raises instead of silently producing out-of-range values.
    if from_ > to:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "uniform_ expects to return a [from, to) range, but found "
            f"from={from_:g} > to={to:g}"
        )
    # The reference writes in place and returns the same tensor.  This
    # implementation must return a distinct tensor, and a contiguous one: a
    # strided ``self`` (e.g. ``base[..., 0]``) has gaps that the four-block
    # store pattern would otherwise leave as uninitialised memory.
    out = torch.empty(self.shape, dtype=self.dtype, device=self.device)
    n = out.numel()
    if n == 0:
        return out
    plan = _plan(self.dtype, n, from_, to)
    block, grid, lo, hi, span = plan[0], plan[1], plan[2], plan[3], plan[4]
    if generator is None:
        generator = torch_device_fn.default_generators[
            self.device.index
            if self.device.index is not None
            else torch_device_fn.current_device()
        ]
    # Lean generator state access: the NPU generator state is [seed, offset]
    # int64 and get_offset/set_offset touch exactly those fields, so this
    # advances the same philox offset as philox_backend_seed_offset (which
    # round-trips the state ByteTensor through tensors) at a fraction of the
    # host cost.  The advance equals the counter range this call consumes.
    seed = generator.initial_seed()
    offset = generator.get_offset()
    generator.set_offset(offset + grid * block)
    execute = plan[5]
    if execute is not None:
        try:
            execute(out, n, seed, offset, self.device.index or 0)
            return out
        except Exception:
            plan[5] = None
    kern = uniform_kernel[(grid,)](out, n, seed, offset, from_, span, lo, hi, BLOCK=block)
    try:
        plan[5] = _direct(kern, block, grid, from_, span, lo, hi)
    except Exception:
        plan[5] = None
    return out

from flag_gems.utils.random_utils import (
    philox_backend_seed_offset,
    uint_to_uniform_float,
)
from flag_gems.utils.shape_utils import volume

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@triton.jit
def _next_below(x, DT: tl.constexpr):
    """Largest ``DT`` value strictly less than ``x``."""
    zero = x == 0
    if DT == tl.float32:
        bits = x.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True)
        step = tl.where(x >= 0, -1, 1).to(tl.int32)
        stepped = (bits + step).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True)
        tiny = tl.full((), 1, tl.int32).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True)
        return tl.where(zero, -tiny, stepped).to(tl.float32)
    elif DT == tl.float64:
        bits = x.to(tl.int64, bitcast=True)
        step = tl.where(x >= 0, -1, 1).to(tl.int64)
        stepped = (bits + step).to(tl.float64, bitcast=True)
        tiny = tl.full((), 1, tl.int64).to(tl.float64, bitcast=True)
        return tl.where(zero, -tiny, stepped).to(tl.float64)
    else:
        bits = x.to(tl.int16, bitcast=True)
        step = tl.where(x >= 0, -1, 1).to(tl.int16)
        stepped = (bits + step).to(DT, bitcast=True)
        tiny = tl.full((), 1, tl.int16).to(DT, bitcast=True)
        return tl.where(zero, -tiny, stepped).to(DT)

def uniform_kernel(
    out_ptr,
    N,
    philox_seed,
    philox_offset,
    from_,
    to,
    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
):
    philox_seed = philox_seed.to(tl.int64)
    philox_offset = philox_offset.to(tl.int64)
    c0 = (philox_offset & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32)
    c1 = ((philox_offset >> 32) & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.uint32)

    r0 = uint_to_uniform_float(r0) * (to - from_) + from_
    r1 = uint_to_uniform_float(r1) * (to - from_) + from_
    r2 = uint_to_uniform_float(r2) * (to - from_) + from_
    r3 = uint_to_uniform_float(r3) * (to - from_) + from_

    from_dt = (r0 * 0.0 + from_).to(OUT_DT)

    r1 = tl.minimum(r1.to(OUT_DT), hi)

    tl.store(out_ptr + off_2, r2, mask=off_2 < N, eviction_policy="evict_first")

conclusion.root_cause: Baseline measured: all 18 workloads pass, geo_mean 0.1520. Latency is flat ~0.350 ms for the three 1024-element cases (fp16/bf16/fp32) and ~0.345-0.351 ms for all three 65536-element cases, but 2.41-2.45 ms for the three 1048576-element cases. The flat 0.35 ms floor across element counts is host-side per-call cost (flag_gems philox_backend_seed_offset reads/writes generator state through device tensors), while the extra ~2.1 ms at 1M elements is the Philox/scale/store device kernel (same magnitude for fp16, bf16 and fp32, so the store conversion is not the driver).
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Baseline only, no prior measurement. Reference walltime is ~0.087-0.131 ms on every case, i.e. the reference call is launch-bound, so the whole gap is our own per-call cost: ~0.25 ms of avoidable host RNG-state work on the small cases and ~2.1 ms of device kernel time on the 1M cases (speedup 0.035-0.045 there).
conclusion.next_suggestion: Use a bounded debug job to read the installed flag_gems random_utils (philox_backend_seed_offset, uint_to_uniform_float) and the ascend _lean_seed_offset helper, time the host state-fetch path against initial_seed/get_offset/set_offset, and time kernel variants (tl.philox vs a manual uint32 Philox4x32-10) to locate the 2.1 ms/1M-element device cost before rewriting.

plan.strategy: Vectorize the Philox device path and remove launch-bound host overhead while repairing the two independent-gate semantic defects (dtype-exact lower clamp, contiguous output for strided input).
plan.code_changes: 1) Replaced tl.philox with a manual vectorized Philox4x32-10 in uint32 arithmetic (16-bit split multiply-high, masked low-word reconstruction) in the same counter/key layout as the seed. 2) Replaced the seed's in-kernel fp32 round-trip bound computation with host-computed, dtype-exact clamp bounds (smallest representable value >= from_, largest < to) passed as two float scalars, then clamped with min/max after the store conversion. 3) Output allocated contiguous via torch.empty(shape, dtype, device) so a strided self is handled. 4) Host RNG state via generator.initial_seed()/get_offset()/set_offset() advancing exactly grid*BLOCK counters, replacing philox_backend_seed_offset. 5) BLOCK = clamp(next_pow2(n/160), 64, 4096) with the heuristics decorator removed, so grid >= ~40 programs for large tensors.
plan.hypothesis: The seed device kernel is dominated by a scalarised tl.philox lowering (~350 us for one 1024-lane program, ~7x350 us for 1M elements) and the per-call host cost by the generator state ByteTensor round-trip; replacing both and fixing the two independent-gate semantic defects (missing nearest-dtype lower clamp, stride-unsafe output allocation) should cut small-case latency from ~0.35 ms toward ~0.13 ms and large-case latency from ~2.45 ms toward ~0.13 ms.

expected_effect.mechanism: The seed spends ~0.25 us per lane inside a scalarised tl.philox (351 us for a single 1024-lane program) plus ~27 us of host RNG-state fetch and a stride-unsafe allocation; a vectorized Philox removes the device cost and the lean state API plus better-shaped blocks cut the launch-bound floor.

def _mul_hi_lo(a, B0: tl.constexpr, B1: tl.constexpr):

    ``B`` is split into 16-bit halves, so only 16x16 and 32x16 products are
    needed instead of a 32x32->64 multiply-high.  The low product falls out of
    the same partial products: the low half-word of ``u0`` and the high
    half-word of the true product are both ``a0*b0``'s low half, and the high
    half-word of the product is ``w1``'s low half, so an xor of ``w1 << 16``
    with ``u0`` reproduces the low 32 bits exactly.
    """
    a0 = a & 0xFFFF
    a1 = a >> 16
    u0 = a0 * B0
    t = a1 * B0 + (u0 >> 16)
    w1 = a0 * B1 + (t & 0xFFFF)
    hi = a1 * B1 + (t >> 16) + (w1 >> 16)
    # low32 = a0*b0 + (a0*b1 + a1*b0) * 2**16 (mod 2**32): its low half is
    # a0*b0's low half and its high half is (a0*b1 + a1*b0 + a0*b0>>16) mod
    # 2**16, which is exactly w1's low half.  Both halves must be placed, not
    # xored into the existing bits of u0.
    lo = (u0 & 0xFFFF) | ((w1 & 0xFFFF) << 16)
    return hi, lo

profile.summary: mixed: Six timing cases are host-bound: the 1024-element call costs 10.77 us of device time inside a 70.02 us eval call, and the device stream idles ~70 us between consecutive kernels, Three 1M-element cases are device-bound and vector-pipe bound: eval latency equals kernel duration, vector ratio 0.88-0.90 with MTE2 ~0 and MTE3 <=2.5%, The 1024-element case runs only 4 programs on a 20-core device, so per-program fixed cost dominates its 10.77 us device time

conclusion.root_cause: Per-call latency was flat at 0.111-0.120 ms independent of element count because the Triton metacall rebuilds bound arguments, specialisation and the cache key on every launch (~62-71 us measured for this 8-argument kernel) on top of ~10-14 us of wrapper Python; the device work was only a few microseconds except at 1M elements.
conclusion.perf_gap_analysis: Frozen expectation was that launch-bound cases would fall at or below the reference's ~0.10 ms; observed 0.0678-0.0705 ms on the six small/medium cases and 0.0853-0.0880 ms on the three 1M cases, so geo_mean rose 0.8924 -> 1.4926 and every workload now beats the reference (min speedup 1.126). The gain is smaller than a naive subtraction of the whole ~70 us metacall, which is consistent with the wrapper's other host work (allocation, generator state, stream query) and with the 1M cases becoming limited by device execution (~85 us) once the host stopped gating them; the large-case speedups 1.13/1.13/1.28 are the new worst three and now reflect kernel time, not host time.
conclusion.next_suggestion: The three 1048576-element cases are now device-bound at 0.085-0.088 ms (speedup 1.13-1.28) while the six smaller cases are 1.6-1.8, so the remaining headroom is in the kernel rather than the launch path: the Philox chain is ten serially dependent rounds per lane, so interleaving two independent counter chains per lane (eight outputs) with a correspondingly smaller BLOCK would expose instruction-level parallelism and could cut the large-case time, at the risk of unified-buffer pressure.
conclusion.debug_lesson: The decisive evidence was the shape of the latency curve, not any single measurement: a flat per-call cost across 1024/65536/1048576 with a ~0.25 us-per-lane spike only for the RNG path identified a scalarised builtin plus a metacall floor. Reading the installed JITFunction.run source gave the exact backend launcher argument layout (9 leading arguments plus all bound arguments including the constexpr), which was the only reliable way to re-enter the compiled kernel without guessing the private ABI.
conclusion.strategy_evolution: Round 1 showed the cost is per-call, not per-element; probes then attributed it (scalarised tl.philox ~0.25 us/lane, state round-trip 27 us, metacall floor ~60 us). Round 2 removed the first two but left a flat ~0.115 ms, which this round's launch-path change removed; the residual split is now visible as 0.068 ms host-bound versus 0.085 ms device-bound at 1M, which redirects the next experiment from host dispatch to kernel ILP.
